# Discovery Loop

## Signal Intake

Teams collect raw signals from interviews, support conversations, observed friction, and field evidence before they commit to a product direction. This opening step matters because early synthesis is often distorted when the team jumps straight from anecdotes to delivery.

## Hypothesis Work

The discovery loop turns customer learning into explicit assumptions, identifies what is still uncertain, and frames small checks that can disconfirm the current story. A good loop uses evidence gathering, hypothesis checks, and lightweight experiments before anyone expands a solution prematurely.

## Decision Framing

The goal is to reduce uncertainty, refine the problem framing, and turn observations into better product decisions. This is the section that matters when the question is how to reduce uncertainty before expanding a solution or how assumption testing should shape the next move.

## Delivery Guard

Discovery is not a license for endless research. The note explains how to stop when the team has enough evidence to decide, while still avoiding the mistake of shipping a larger solution before the core assumption has been tested.
